mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST decreases > 10% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS decreases > 5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market with high interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing and real GDP (GDPC1) is decreasing, it signals a supply-side driven economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases and GDPC1 decreases.
